supporting_quotes: Abstract—Text-to-Speech (TTS) has recently seen great progress in synthesizing high-quality speech owing to the rapid development of parallel TTS systems.
Here, we propose StyleTTS, a style-based generative model for parallel TTS that can synthesize diverse speech with natural prosody from a reference speech utterance.

This paper presents the following novel contributions: (i) the introduction of the Transferable Monotonic Aligner (TMA), a new transfer learning scheme that refines pre-trained text aligners for TTS tasks, (ii) a duration-invariant data augmentation method for improving prosody prediction, and (iii) a parallel TTS model that incorporates generalized speech styles for natural and expressive speech synthesis.

The structure of parallel TTS models allows for the entire speech to be synthesized, presenting an opportunity to leverage the powerful AdaIN module for integrating generalized styles in diverse speech synthesis.

supporting_quotes: Abstract—Recent single-channel speech enhancement methods based on deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable results, but there are still generalization problems in real scenes.

In this study, we make full use of the contribution of multi-target joint learning to the model generalization capability, and propose a lightweight and low-computing dilated convolutional network (DCN) model for a more robust speech denoising task.
To do this, we build a multi-stage learning framework to deal with multiple targets in stages to achieve their joint learning, namely ‘MT-in-MS’.
The remainder of this paper is structured as follows.
The formulation of multi-targets is presented in Section 2.
Section 3 describes the multi-stage learning framework.
